statement: Let n >= 4 and let K be a characteristic-zero field. In the n-Lie matched-pair structure of Example 8.7 fixed in source.md and problem.md, write a linear map r: V -> g in the stated column convention as R = [[A,v],[w^T,alpha]]. Then r is a deformation map if and only if det(A) v = 0 and det(R) = alpha det(A). Equivalently, when det(A) != 0 one has v = 0 with w and alpha arbitrary, while when det(A) = 0 the sole condition is det(R) = 0.
contribution: This is a complete proof of the frozen all-matrices classification. It specializes Definition 7.1 without discarded terms, identifies both sides as determinant-valued alternating maps, audits the cofactor sign for arbitrary n, and proves necessity and sufficiency. The cited source exhibits one deformation map rather than this classification. No novelty or priority claim is made because full-text comparison with the 2022 ternary predecessor remains unverified.
